subject: Stakeholder sync: procurement route decision and SOC 2 gating
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@brightpath.health>, Procurement Team <procure@brightpath.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder sync — procurement route decision and SOC 2 gating

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the 8:30 call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can prioritize the right paper path. High-level notes:

- Desire: BrightPath wants Redwood for inference across a subset of patient-facing workflows. Legal and procurement asked whether we can do this via marketplace provisioning vs a direct PO/paperflow.
- Security gating: procurement flagged SOC 2 Type II evidence and a signed DPA as hard prerequisites before vendor approval. They also mentioned the security questionnaire (third-party) will be sent this week and may request specific answers about data residency and retention.
- Commercial preference: procurement indicated they prefer marketplace to avoid long SOW/PO cycles, but the business (Alex) prefers direct contract if it gives faster entitlement for production tokens and a fixed committed spend.

Immediate asks / next steps (please confirm owners & ETA):
1) Priya (me): Share a concise SOC 2 summary + our standard DPA template and a short note on what parts of the security questionnaire we can answer immediately — ETA EOD today (I will attach SOC2 summary).
2) Alex / Procurement: Confirm whether marketplace provisioning is an option for your security/compliance team (procurement to confirm internal approval path) — reply by Tue 05/04 if possible.
3) Ben: Given the likelihood of marketplace vs direct PO, can you prepare two commercial sketches: (A) marketplace SKU pricing with expected lead time to entitlement, (B) draft PO/SOW commercial terms (monthly commit + overage) — ETA Wed 05/05.
4) Karthik: If procurement pushes for on-prem or VPC later, flag any technical blockers or a rough timeline for Private deployment onboarding.

Attachments: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (PDF, 280KB) — high-level controls map; Draft-SOW-Redwood-v0.3.docx (stub) included as a starting point for negotiations.

Goal: get procurement to confirm preferred route (marketplace vs PO) this week so we can line up the right paperwork and legal review.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan

Thanks Priya — that recap is perfect. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Marketplace is attractive because it reduces time to start trials (fewer internal approvals), but our security reviewers have historically required supplemental vendor evidence even for marketplace vendors (SOC 2 upload + DPA). So marketplace may not completely avoid paperwork.
- Procurement will try to evaluate marketplace first for a proof-of-concept (low-risk pilot). If the pilot expands, we will likely need a PO or a master services agreement to get committed pricing.
- The security questionnaire will be shared with you (procurement said "by EOD Monday") — expect a vendor questionnaire form and a separate section for data residency.

I'll confirm by Tue whether procurement approves marketplace for the pilot. For timeline, our PM wants a 30-day trial window starting mid-May if we can provision quickly.

Best,
Alex
Alex Jordan
Director of Product, BrightPath Health
alex.jordan@brightpath.health

Good notes — quick commercial sketches below. I can put formal numbers in a one-pager tomorrow.

A) Marketplace pilot (fastest):
- Off-the-shelf SKU: per-token pricing with standard marketplace fees; no custom SOW required.
- Lead time: typically 3–7 business days for entitlement if marketplace onboarding is straightforward.
- Tradeoff: limited ability to negotiate committed discounts and data processing terms; we can still supply a DPA uploaded to marketplace vendor console.

B) Direct PO / SOW (more control):
- Model: monthly committed capacity with overage; 30–60 day legal review depending on counterparty load.
- Lead time: 2–4 weeks for procurement + legal for a simple PO/SOW; longer if custom security addenda required.
- Tradeoff: better pricing predictability and ability to include a Redwood-hosted Private option later.

Risk notes for procurement:
- Security questionnaire: if they ask for SOC 2 Type II evidence + console access for audit traces, we can provide a redacted report and a CSV of audit log retention policy; legal will need to review the redactions.
- DPA: Redwood standard DPA is compatible with most customers; if they require additional clauses around patient data we will need legal to sign off (may add 1–2 weeks).

I'll prepare two short attachments: Marketplace-quote.pdf and PO-SOW-sketch.pdf by Wed 05/05. If procurement confirms marketplace pilot, we can fast-track entitlement and push the PO route as the expansion path.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses. Two quick clarifications and a proposed short timeline:

1) I uploaded SOC2-summary-2026.pdf here and attached the Draft SOW stub; these should answer the immediate auditor questions (controls map + retention policy). If Procurement can confirm marketplace acceptance for a pilot by Tue 05/04, Ben and I will queue a marketplace onboarding and share the marketplace SKU and entitlement checklist.

2) If Procurement prefers PO/SOW, Ben will circulate the PO-SOW-sketch (ETA Wed) and Legal will be looped for the DPA + any custom redlines — expect an additional 7–14 business days for review in the worst case.

Proposed near-term timeline:
- Mon 05/03: Procurement sends vendor questionnaire (if not already sent).
- Tue 05/04: Procurement confirms marketplace vs PO preference for pilot.
- Wed 05/05: Redwood shares commercial sketches (marketplace SKU + PO sketch).
- Fri 05/07: Redwood and BrightPath align on pilot start window (goal: mid-May).

If procurement has a hard SOC 2 Type II upload requirement before any marketplace entitlement, please flag that explicitly — we'll prioritize getting the full report redacted and uploaded, but legal will need visibility on the redactions.

Thanks — looping Karthik for any notes on Private/VPC considerations in case the business wants to bake that into the SOW.

Best,
Priya
